engineering_notes: Pinned DSDG files are imported unchanged from the verified source cache via methods.common.upstream.upstream_modules (networks, misc.util only; train_generator/data are not imported).

misc/util.py::reparameterize uses the legacy torch.cuda.FloatTensor(size).normal_() constructor; torch 2.12.1 executes it unchanged with a deprecation UserWarning. Distribution and RNG (global CUDA default generator) are unchanged.
train_generator.py:154-157 F.interpolate(mode='bilinear') passes no align_corners; the default is align_corners=False in both PyTorch 1.6 and 2.12, so interpolation semantics are unchanged.

The upstream LightCNN loader (train_generator.py:75-84) lives inside main(); the harness mirrors its filter/update/load/freeze statements. torch>=2.6 defaults torch.load(weights_only=True); it is passed explicitly. The legacy file needs only OrderedDict/FloatStorage/_rebuild_tensor, so the loaded tensors are identical (asserted by torch.equal) and no pickled code executes.
cudnn.benchmark=False/deterministic=True follow the frozen M6C2a seed_plan, not upstream cudnn.benchmark=True; this is a runtime control, not a model semantic.
TMPDIR is redirected into the dedicated build root so the Python write firewall needs no /tmp exception.

identity.compiler: NOT_USED: no extension build; pinned DSDG uses standard torch.nn operators only

selection_rationale: Historical upstream Python 3.8 / PyTorch 1.6.0 / torchvision 0.7.0 are provenance only: PyTorch 1.6 CUDA 10.x builds ship no sm_86 kernels for the RTX 3090 (capability 8.6). The pinned DSDG generator/LightCNN use only standard torch.nn operators and no custom extension, so the already-qualified modern CUDA 13.0 stack of gpat-m5 is the minimal compatible runtime; no version was chosen to change model size or memory.
